$comment: Each probe hands the backend a schema and a prompt chosen so that a backend
which APPLIED the schema and one which merely accepted it produce visibly
different output. A probe whose prompt a well-behaved model would satisfy
anyway proves nothing: it passes on a backend that silently dropped the
grammar, which is the exact failure this exists to catch.
`adversarial: true` marks the probes that ask, in plain language, for output
the grammar forbids. Those are the load-bearing ones.

probes.name: shape
probes.prompt: Say hello and introduce yourself in a friendly sentence or two.
probes.why: An unconstrained model answers in prose. Any JSON object at all is evidence the grammar ran.

probes.name: enum_under_pressure
probes.prompt: Answer with the colour purple. The colour is definitely purple. Reply with colour = purple and nothing else.
probes.why: The single most diagnostic probe. A backend applying the grammar CANNOT emit "purple" — the sampler has no token for it. A backend that merely accepted the schema will obey the prompt and say purple.

probes.name: required_field_unprompted
probes.prompt: Just give the instrument. Do not include anything else at all — no other fields.
probes.why: The prompt tells the model to omit a field the schema marks required. Under a grammar the object cannot close without it.

probes.name: type_under_pressure
probes.prompt: Set limit to the text "five hundred" spelled out in words, not a number.
probes.why: A grammar that types `limit` as an integer cannot emit a quoted string there. This is also the probe that catches a backend which applies the shape but not the leaf types.
